Dissemination Seminar to raise the awareness of the reporting entities on “Anti-Money laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism and the Financing of Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction”
11 August 2026 9:07:11 PM
On the morning of Tuesday, 11th August 2026, the Insurance Regulator of Cambodia (IRC) organized a dissemination seminar to raise the awareness of the reporting entities on “Anti-Money laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism and the Financing of Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction”, presided over by Dr. HOR Sovathana, Deputy Director General of IRC, highly representative of H.E. BOU Chanphirou, Director General of IRC, with participation from representatives of Cambodia Financial Intelligence Unit, General Commissariat of National Police, IRC’s officials as well as representatives of the Insurance Association of Cambodia and reporting entities of the insurance sector in Cambodia.

ពិធីប្រគល់មូលនិធិសប្បុរសធម៌របស់ ក្រុមហ៊ុន ដាយ អ៊ិឈិ ឡាយហ្វ៍ អ៊ីនសួរ៉ិនស៍ (ខេមបូឌា) ជូនដល់មជ្ឈមណ្ឌលកុមារបេះដូងជប៉ុន
៧ មិថុនា ២០២៤ ៩:៤១:៥៨ ល្ងាច
នៅព្រឹកថ្ងៃសុក្រ ១កើត ខែជេស្ឋ ឆ្នាំរោង ឆស័ក ព.ស.២៥៦៨ ត្រូវនឹងថ្ងៃទី៧ ខែមិថុនា គ.ស.២០២៤ លោកស្រីបណ្ឌិត ហោ សុវឌ្ឍនា អគ្គនាយករងនៃនិយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា (ន.ធ.ក. នៅព្រឹកថ្ងៃពុធ ៧រោច ខែទុតិយាសាឍ ឆ្នាំមមី អដ្ឋស័ក ព.ស.២៥៧០ ត្រូវនឹងថ្ងៃទី៥ ខែសីហា គ.ស.២០២៦ ឯកឧត្តម ប៊ូ ច័ន្ទភីរូ អគ្គនាយក នៃនិយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា (ន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា)) បានអញ្ជើញជាអធិបតីក្នុងសិក្ខាសាលាស្តីពី “ដំណើរឆ្ពោះទៅរកការអនុវត្តស្តង់ដាររបាយការណ៍ហិរញ្ញវត្ថុអន្តរជាតិលេខ១៧៖ បទពិសោធន៍ បញ្ហាប្រឈម និងទស្សនៈវិស័យរបស់វិស័យធានារ៉ាប់រង” ដែលជាការរៀបចំឡើងដោយសមាគមធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា នៅសណ្ឋាគារភ្នំពេញ ដោយមានការអញ្ជើញចូលរួមពីសមាជិកក្រុមការងារជំរុញការអនុវត្តស្តង់ដារបាយការណ៍ហិរញ្ញវត្ថុអន្តរជាតិនៅក្នុងវិស័យធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា និងតំណាងក្រុមហ៊ុនធានារ៉ាប់រងក្នុងព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា។

ព័ត៌មានថ្មីៗ
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមការងារអនុរដ្ឋមន្ត្រីហិរញ្ញវត្ថុ និងធនាគារកណ្ដាលអាស៊ាន (AFCDM-WG) និងកិច្ចប្រជុំពាក់ព័ន្ធ
១៥ កុម្ភៈ ២០២៦ ៨:១០:២៦ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំពិគ្រោះយោបល់លើសេចក្តីព្រាងប្រកាសស្តីពី “ការដាក់ឱ្យប្រើប្រាស់បណ្ណសន្យារ៉ាប់រងភារៈទទួលខុសត្រូវយានយន្តជាកាតព្វកិច្ច” និងសេចក្តីព្រាងប្រកាសស្តីពី “ការកំណត់បុព្វលាភធានារ៉ាប់រងភារៈទទួលខុសត្រូវយានយន្តជាកាតព្វកិច្ច”
១១ កុម្ភៈ ២០២៦ ១០:៤៨:០៣ ព្រឹក
កិច្ចប្រជុំពិភាក្សាលើបញ្ហាប៊េងកាសួរេន
១០ កុម្ភៈ ២០២៦ ១:១៩:៣០ ល្ងាច
សន្និបាតបូកសរុបលទ្ធផលការងារប្រចាំឆ្នាំ២០២៥ និងលើកទិសដៅការងារសម្រាប់ឆ្នាំ២០២៦
៦ កុម្ភៈ ២០២៦ ៥:៤៩:២០ ព្រឹក
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមប្រឹក្សាភិបាលអាស៊ានតាក់សូណូមី (The ASEAN Taxonomy Board - ATB)
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមប្រឹក្សាភិបាលអាស៊ានតាក់សូណូមី (The ASEAN Taxonomy Board - ATB)
២៦ មករា ២០២៦ ៨:៤៧:៤០ ព្រឹក
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមប្រឹក្សាអាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ (អ.ស.ហ. (អាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ)) អាណត្តិទី១ លើកទី២៨
៧ មករា ២០២៦ ១០:៣១:៤៩ ព្រឹក
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមប្រឹក្សា អ.ស.ហ. (អាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ) អាណត្តិទី១ លើកទី២៧
២៤ ធ្នូ ២០២៥ ៨:៣៩:០៤ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី “គោលការណ៍ណែនាំស្តីពីក្រមសីលធម៌បុគ្គលវិជ្ជាជីវៈជើងសាធារ៉ាប់រង”
១៣ ធ្នូ ២០២៥ ៨:៥១:៤៩ ព្រឹក
កិច្ចប្រជុំជាន់ខ្ពស់អាស៊ី-ប៉ាស៊ីហ្វិក នៃ AFIR-FSI-IAIS (HLM) លើការត្រួតពិនិត្យធានារ៉ាប់រងលើកទី៨ និងកិច្ចប្រជុំប្រចាំឆ្នាំរបស់វេទិកានិយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងអាស៊ីលើកទី២០ (AMS)
១៣ ធ្នូ ២០២៥ ៨:៤៩:៤២ ព្រឹក
ពិធីប្រកាសដាក់ឱ្យដំណើរការជាផ្លូវការ “ប្រព័ន្ធទទួលបណ្តឹងធានារ៉ាប់រងតាមកម្មវិធីទូរសព្ទដៃ”
១១ ធ្នូ ២០២៥ ៣:១៥:៤៩ ល្ងាច

ការប្រគល់សម្ភារព័ត៌មានវិទ្យាទៅ សាលាបឋមសិក្សាចំនួន២ ក្នុងឃុំកំពង់អុស
២៩ មេសា ២០២៤ ៨:២១:៥៣ ព្រឹក
នៅព្រឹកថ្ងៃសៅរ៍៤រោច ខែចេត្រ ឆ្នាំរោង ឆស័ក ព.ស.២៥៦៧ ត្រូវនឹងថ្ងៃទី២៧ ខែមេសា គ.ស.២០២៤ និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា (ន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា)) បាននាំយកសម្ភារព័ត៌មានវិទ្យារួមមាន កុំព្យូរទ័រលើតុ និងម៉ាស៊ីនបោះពុម្ពប្រគល់ជូនសាលាបឋមសិក្សាជ្រៃអណ្តែត និងសាលាបឋមសិក្សាព្រហ្មក្តុរ ស្ថិតក្នុងឃុំកំពង់អុស ស្រុកពញ្ញាឮ ខេត្តកណ្តាល ដើម្បីជួយសម្រួលដល់កិច្ចការរដ្ឋបាលប្រចាំថ្ងៃ ។

និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា - Insurance Regulator of Cambodia (ន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា) - IRC)
ពិធីដើរកម្សាន្ត ២៧០០ ជំហានដើម្បីទារក និងកុមារកម្ពុជា
៥ មិថុនា ២០២៦ ១១:២៩:១៤ ព្រឹក
នៅរសៀលថ្ងៃព្រហស្បតិ៍ ៤រោច ខែជេស្ឋ ឆ្នាំមមី អដ្ឋស័ក ព.ស.២៥៧០ ត្រូវនឹងថ្ងៃទី៤ ខែមិថុនា គ.ស.២០២៦ ឯកឧត្តម ប៊ូ ច័ន្ទភីរូ អគ្គនាយកនៃនិយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា (ន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា)) បានអញ្ជើញចូលរួមក្នុង “ពិធីដើរកម្សាន្ត ២៧០០ ជំហានដើម្បីទារក និងកុមារកម្ពុជា” ក្រោមអធិបតីភាពដ៏ខ្ពង់ខ្ពស់ ឯកឧត្តមអគ្គបណ្ឌិតសភាចារ្យ អូន ព័ន្ធមុនីរ័ត្ន ឧបនាយករដ្ឋមន្រ្តី រដ្ឋមន្រ្តីក្រសួងសេដ្ឋកិច្ច និងហិរញ្ញវត្ថុ និងជាប្រធានក្រុមប្រឹក្សាបរធនបាលនៃមូលនិធិគន្ធបុប្ផាកម្ពុជា ដែលបានធ្វើឡើងនៅពហុកីឡដ្ឋានជាតិមរតកតេជោ ។
និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា
ប្រព័ន្ធ​ផ្សព្វផ្សាយ​សង្គម

ព័ត៌មានថ្មីៗ
ពិធីចុះអនុស្សរណៈនៃការយោគយល់គ្នារវាង ន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា) និង ស.ជ.ម.
១៩ សីហា ២០២៥ ១១:០៨:២៧ ព្រឹក
កិច្ចប្រជុំតាមដាន ត្រួតពិនិត្យ និងវាយតម្លៃ ការអនុវត្តផែនការអភិវឌ្ឍន៍ស្ថាប័នបច្ចុប្បន្នកម្មរបស់ន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា) រយៈពេល ១០ឆ្នាំ
១៥ សីហា ២០២៥ ១១:០៨:៤៨ ព្រឹក
សិក្ខាសាលាសាធារណៈស្តីពី "បច្ចុប្បន្នភាពវិស័យធានារ៉ាប់រងនៅកម្ពុជា"ជូនដល់និស្សិតសាកលវិទ្យាល័យកម្ពុជា
៣១ កក្កដា ២០២៥ ៨:១៦:០២ ព្រឹក
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី “លិខិតបទដ្ឋានគតិយុត្តស្តីពីការធានារ៉ាប់រង” នៅខេត្តកំពង់ចាម
២៨ កក្កដា ២០២៥ ៩:០៩:១៦ ល្ងាច
បាឋកថាស្តីពី “វិស័យធានារ៉ាប់រងក្នុងសេដ្ឋកិច្ច និងទីផ្សារការងារ”នៅសាកលវិទ្យាល័យជាតិជាស៊ីមកំចាយមារ
២៨ កក្កដា ២០២៥ ៤:១៣:០៣ ល្ងាច
ពិធីចុះអនុស្សរណៈនៃការយោគយល់គ្នារវាងន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា) និងសាកលវិទ្យាល័យ ហេង សំរិន ត្បូងឃ្មុំ
២៦ កក្កដា ២០២៥ ៩:០៣:៥៤ ល្ងាច
វេទិកានិយ័តករនិងអគ្គនាយកធានារ៉ាប់រង
២៥ កក្កដា ២០២៥ ៣:៤២:០៧ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយអំពី “ផលិតផលធានារ៉ាប់រងខ្នាតលើដំណាំកសិកម្ម” ខេត្តបាត់ដំបង
១៨ កក្កដា ២០២៥ ៨:៥៧:២៨ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំប្រចាំឆមាសទី១ គ.ស.២០២៥
១៤ កក្កដា ២០២៥ ១០:០២:៣៨ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាស្តីពី "ការយល់ដឹងអំពីការអនុវត្តជាក់ស្តែង និងនិន្នាការនៃការអនុវត្តក្នុងតំបន់ នៃស្តង់ដារបាយការណ៍ហិរញ្ញវត្ថុអន្តរជាតិ លេខ១៧"

Seminar on “Compulsory Insurance” at Takeo Province
28 July 2026 4:24:52 PM
On the morning of Tuesday, 28 July 2026, Insurance Regulator of Cambodia (IRC) organized a dissemination seminar on “Compulsory Insurance” at Takeo Province, presided over by Dr. HOR Sovathana, Deputy Director General of the IRC, highly representative of H.E. BOU Chanphirou, Director General of the IRC, with participation from Mr. MAM Kay, Deputy Governor of Takeo Province, and attended by the Inter-Ministerial Working Group, relevant provincial departments/ institutions, competent authorities, and related private institutions in the province.

ព័ត៌មានថ្មីៗ
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី"ផលិតផលធានារ៉ាប់រងយានយន្ត" និង "ផលិតផលធានារ៉ាប់រងសុខភាព" នៅខេត្តប៉ៃលិន
២៩ ឧសភា ២០២៥ ៩:២៤:២៨ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី “លិខិតបទដ្ឋានគតិយុត្តស្តីពីការធានារ៉ាប់រង” នៅខេត្តបន្ទាយមានជ័យ
២៣ ឧសភា ២០២៥ ៩:១៨:០៤ ល្ងាច
បាឋកថាស្តីពី “វិស័យធានារ៉ាប់រងក្នុងសេដ្ឋកិច្ច និងទីផ្សារការងារ”នៅសាកលវិទ្យាល័យជាតិមានជ័យ
២៣ ឧសភា ២០២៥ ៩:០៨:០៤ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមប្រឹក្សាអាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារអាណត្តិទី១ លើកទី២៤
២១ ឧសភា ២០២៥ ១០:៥៨:០២ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំលើកទី១០ ស្តីពីការដឹកជញ្ជូនតាមផ្លូវថ្នល់ រវាងប្រទេសកម្ពុជា និងវៀតណាម
២១ ឧសភា ២០២៥ ១០:៥០:១៤ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី “បែបបទ និងនីតិវិធីនៃការដាក់ទណ្ឌកម្មចំពោះបុគ្គលប្រព្រឹត្តល្មើសនឹងច្បាប់ ឬលិខិតបទដ្ឋានគតិយុត្តក្នុងវិស័យធានារ៉ាប់រង”
១៣ ឧសភា ២០២៥ ៩:១២:២២ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមការងារអន្តរក្រសួងដើម្បីអនុវត្តប្រកាសអន្តរក្រសួងស្តីពីកាតព្វកិច្ចធានារ៉ាប់រងលើកទី៨
៨ ឧសភា ២០២៥ ២:១១:២៦ ល្ងាច
“ទិវាធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា ២០២៥” ខេត្តបាត់ដំបង
២៨ មេសា ២០២៥ ១២:១៧:២៦ ព្រឹក
វេទិកាចែករំលែកព័ត៌មានអំពី “បច្ចុប្បន្នភាពនៃទីផ្សារធានារ៉ាប់រងនៅកម្ពុជា”
២២ មេសា ២០២៥ ៩:៥៥:៣៦ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំប្រចាំត្រីមាសទី១ គ.ស.២០២៥ របស់ ន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា)

សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី"ផលិតផលធានារ៉ាប់រងយានយន្ត" និង "ផលិតផលធានារ៉ាប់រងសុខភាព" នៅខេត្តប៉ៃលិន

21 September 2024 9:20:34 PM

កិច្ចប្រជុំប្រចាំត្រីមាសទី១ នៃគ.ស.២០២៦
៩ មេសា ២០២៦ ៤:០៥:៥៤ ល្ងាច
បាឋកថាស្តីពី “វិស័យធានារ៉ាប់រងក្នុងសេដ្ឋកិច្ច និងទីផ្សារការងារ” នៅសាកលវិទ្យាល័យអង្គរ ខេត្តសៀមរាប
២ មេសា ២០២៦ ៩:៥០:០៧ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី “ការធានារ៉ាប់រងជាកាតព្វកិច្ច” នៅខេត្តសៀមរាប
១ មេសា ២០២៦ ៤:០២:៣៤ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមការងារអន្តរក្រសួងដើម្បីអនុវត្តប្រកាសអន្តរក្រសួងស្តីពីកាតព្វកិច្ចធានារ៉ាប់រងលើកទី១១
២៦ មីនា ២០២៦ ៨:២៩:២០ ល្ងាច

ព័ត៌មានថ្មីៗ
វេទិកា “ធានារ៉ាប់រងឌីជីថលក្នុងតំបន់អាស៊ីប៉ាស៊ីហ្វិកឆ្នាំ២០២៤ (Digital Insurance APAC 2024)” នៅទីក្រុងហុងកុង
២៧ មិថុនា ២០២៤ ៨:៥៧:៣៩ ល្ងាច
ទស្សនកិច្ចសិក្សាអំពីស្តង់ដារបាយការណ៍ហិរញ្ញវត្ថុទី១៧ កិច្ចសន្យាធានារ៉ាប់រង (IFRS17) នៅទីក្រុងហុងកុង
២០ មិថុនា ២០២៤ ៤:១៦:៤៧ ល្ងាច
វគ្គបណ្តុះបណ្តាលអំពីសេវាសាធារណៈរបស់ន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា)
១៩ មិថុនា ២០២៤ ៨:០៩:០០ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយអំពី "ផលិតផលធានារ៉ាប់រងខ្នាតតូច" នៅខេត្តព្រៃវែង
១៧ មិថុនា ២០២៤ ៩:៣៩:៤៩ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្ដីពី “បទប្បញ្ញត្តិប្រុងប្រយ័ត្ន” នៅខេត្តព្រះសីហនុ
១៣ មិថុនា ២០២៤ ៩:៥០:០៥ ល្ងាច

ព័ត៌មានថ្មីៗ
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយ “ផែនការយុទ្ធសាស្ត្រអភិវឌ្ឍន៍វិស័យធានារ៉ាប់រង ២០២១-២០៣០”
៧ មិថុនា ២០២៤ ៩:៣២:៤៨ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាពិគ្រោះយោបល់លើសេចក្តីព្រាងប្រកាសស្តីពី“លតាបត្រធានារ៉ាប់រងភារៈទទួលខុសត្រូវយានយន្ត និងភារៈទទួលខុសត្រូវការដឹកជញ្ជូនអ្នកដំណើរ”
៤ មិថុនា ២០២៤ ១០:០៤:២២ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំពិគ្រោះយោបល់ស្តីពី "ទម្រង់របាយការណ៍ប្រចាំខែរបស់ក្រុមហ៊ុនធានារ៉ាប់រង"
៣ មិថុនា ២០២៤ ៩:៤៥:០១ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយអំពី "អត្ថប្រយោជន៍នៃផលិតផលធានារ៉ាប់រងអាយុជីវិត" នៅខេត្តតាកែវ
២៧ ឧសភា ២០២៤ ៩:៣២:៣៣ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្ដីពី “វិធានការយកចិត្តទុកដាក់ស្គាល់អតិថិជនសម្រាប់ក្រុមហ៊ុនធានារ៉ាប់រងទូទៅ”
២៤ ឧសភា ២០២៤ ៤:១២:៣៨ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាពិគ្រោះយោបល់លើសេចក្តីព្រាងប្រកាសស្តីពី “លក្ខខណ្ឌ និងនីតិវិធីនៃការបន្ត ការផ្អាក និងការបញ្ចប់កិច្ចសន្យាធានារ៉ាប់រង”
២០ ឧសភា ២០២៤ ៨:០៩:២៤ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី “ការធានារ៉ាប់រងជាកាតព្វកិច្ច” នៅខេត្តកំពង់ចាម
១៧ ឧសភា ២០២៤ ៨:៤៦:៣៤ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមការងារអន្តរក្រសួងដើម្បីអនុវត្តប្រកាសអន្តរក្រសួងស្តីពីកាតព្វកិច្ចធានារ៉ាប់រងលើកទី៥
២៩ មេសា ២០២៤ ១:២៥:០៦ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្ដីពី “នីតិវិធីនៃការទទួល និងដោះស្រាយបណ្តឹងធានារ៉ាប់រង”
២៦ មេសា ២០២៤ ៩:៤៥:២៣ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយអំពី "ផលិតផលធានារ៉ាប់រងខ្នាតតូចលើដំណាំកសិកម្ម"
២៦ មេសា ២០២៤ ៧:២៩:៤៥ ព្រឹក
1

"អត្ថប្រយោជន៍នៃការមានធានារ៉ាប់រងយានយន្ត"
១៥ កុម្ភៈ ២០២៣ ៨:៤៧:៥៨ ព្រឹក

ព័ត៌មានថ្មីៗ
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី “ការធានារ៉ាប់រងជាកាតព្វកិច្ច”
៧ កុម្ភៈ ២០២៥ ៣:៣៤:៤២ ល្ងាច
អនុស្សរណៈនៃការយោគយល់គ្នារវាងនិយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា និងនាយកដ្ឋានត្រួតពិនិត្យសហគ្រាសគ្រប់គ្រងដោយរដ្ឋនិងធានារ៉ាប់រង នៃក្រសួងហិរញ្ញវត្ថុឡាវ
៤ កុម្ភៈ ២០២៥ ៤:០៤:២៧ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្ទៀងផ្ទាត់ស្ដីអំពីការសិក្សាលើធានារ៉ាប់រងប្រកបដោយបរិយាបន្ន និងហិរញ្ញប្បទានហានិភ័យនៅកម្ពុជា
២៩ មករា ២០២៥ ៤:១២:៣៣ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំបូកសរុបសមិទ្ធផលការងារប្រចាំគ.ស.២០២៤ និងលើកទិសដៅការងារបន្ត
២៣ មករា ២០២៥ ៩:២២:១១ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាស្តីពីការស្វែងយល់អំពីដំណើរឆ្ពោះទៅអនុវត្តស្តង់ដារបាយការណ៍ហិរញ្ញវត្ថុអន្តរជាតិលេខ ១៧
១៤ មករា ២០២៥ ៣:៣១:២៦ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមប្រឹក្សា អ.ស.ហ. (អាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ) អាណត្តិទី១ លើកទី២១
២៧ ធ្នូ ២០២៤ ៨:៥៣:៣៣ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំពិគ្រោះយោបល់លើសេចក្តីព្រាងប្រកាសស្តីពី “ការកំណត់បុព្វលាភធានារ៉ាប់រងភារៈទទួលខុសត្រូវយានយន្តជាកាតព្វកិច្ច”
២៤ ធ្នូ ២០២៤ ៨:៥១:០១ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមការងារអន្តរក្រសួងដើម្បីអនុវត្តប្រកាសអន្តរក្រសួងស្តីពីកាតព្វកិច្ចធានារ៉ាប់រងលើកទី៧

សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី “ការធានារ៉ាប់រងជាកាតព្វកិច្ច” នៅខេត្តតាកែវ
២៨ កក្កដា ២០២៦ ៤:២៤:៥២ ល្ងាច
នៅព្រឹកថ្ងៃអង្គារ ១៤កើត ខែទុតិយាសាឍ ឆ្នាំមមី អដ្ឋស័ ព.ស.២៥៧០ ត្រូវនឹងថ្ងៃទី២៨ ខែកក្កដា គ.ស.២០២៦, និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា (ន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា)) បានរៀបចំសិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី “ការធានារ៉ាប់រងជាកាតព្វកិច្ច” នៅខេត្តតាកែវ ក្រោមអធិបតីភាពរបស់ លោកស្រីបណ្ឌិត ហោ សុវឌ្ឍនា អគ្គនាយករង នៃន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា) តំណាងដ៏ខ្ពង់ខ្ពស់ ឯកឧត្តម ប៊ូ ច័ន្ទភីរូ អគ្គនាយកនៃន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា) ដោយមានការអញ្ជើញចូលរួមជាអធិបតីពីលោកម៉ម កាយ អភិបាលរង នៃគណៈអភិបាលខេត្តតាកែវ និងមានចូលរួមពីតំណាងសមាជិកក្រុមការងារអន្តរក្រសួង តំណាងមន្ទីរ អាជ្ញាធរមានសមត្ថកិច្ច គ្រឹះស្ថានឯកជន និងស្ថាប័នពាក់ព័ន្ធក្នុងខេត្តផងដែរ។

ព័ត៌មានថ្មីៗ
កិច្ចប្រជុំអនុគណៈកម្មាធិការទទួលបន្ទុកការគ្របដណ្ដប់សុខភាពជាសកលនៅកម្ពុជា
២០ សីហា ២០២៦ ៩:១៥:៤៤ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំរវាងវេទិកាទីផ្សារមូលធនអាស៊ាននិងក្រុមប្រឹក្សាភិបាលអាស៊ានតាក់សូណូមីលើកទី៣ និងសិក្ខាសាលាក្រោមក្របខណ្ឌ mARs
២០ សីហា ២០២៦ ១:១៤:១៩ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមប្រឹក្សា អ.ស.ហ. (អាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ) លើកទី១ អាណត្តិទី២
១៧ សីហា ២០២៦ ៩:០៦:៤៤ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយអំពីប្រកាសស្តីពី “កិច្ចការពារអ្នកប្រើប្រាស់សេវាធានារ៉ាប់រង”
១១ សីហា ២០២៦ ៩:១៤:០៣ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាលើកកម្ពស់ការយល់ដឹងដល់បុគ្គលរាយការណ៍អំពី “ការប្រឆាំងការសម្អាតប្រាក់និងហិរញ្ញប្បទានភេរវកម្ម និងហិរញ្ញប្បទានដល់ការរីកសាយភាយអាវុធមហាប្រល័យ”
១១ សីហា ២០២៦ ៩:០៧:១១ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំពិគ្រោះយោបល់សេចក្តីព្រាងគោលការណ៍ណែនាំស្តីពីកិច្ចព្រមព្រៀងអន្តរការីធានារ៉ាប់រង
៦ សីហា ២០២៦ ៩:១០:១៥ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាស្តីពីការផ្ទៀងផ្ទាត់ផែនការការងារនៃយុទ្ធសាស្ត្រអាស៊ានសម្រាប់អព្យាក្រឹតកាបូន
៦ សីហា ២០២៦ ១:៣៤:៣៦ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាស្តីពី “ដំណើរឆ្ពោះទៅរកការអនុវត្តស្តង់ដាររបាយការណ៍ហិរញ្ញវត្ថុអន្តរជាតិលេខ១៧៖ បទពិសោធន៍ បញ្ហាប្រឈម និងទស្សនៈវិស័យរបស់វិស័យធានារ៉ាប់រង”
៥ សីហា ២០២៦ ១១:៣៩:៤៦ ព្រឹក
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី “ការធានារ៉ាប់រងជាកាតព្វកិច្ច” នៅខេត្តតាកែវ

វេទិកានិយ័តករ និងអគ្គនាយកធានារ៉ាប់រង ២០២៦

Category: news
Publish date: 2026-08-11 14:14:03.100 UTC

Category: news
Publish date: 2026-08-11 14:07:11.427 UTC

Category: news
Publish date: 2026-08-06 14:10:15.037 UTC
សិក្ខាសាលាស្តីពីការផ្ទៀងផ្ទាត់ផែនការការងារនៃយុទ្ធសាស្ត្រអាស៊ានសម្រាប់អព្យាក្រឹតកាបូន
Category: news
Publish date: 2026-08-06 06:34:36.324 UTC
សិក្ខាសាលាស្តីពី “ដំណើរឆ្ពោះទៅរកការអនុវត្តស្តង់ដាររបាយការណ៍ហិរញ្ញវត្ថុអន្តរជាតិលេខ១៧៖ បទពិសោធន៍ បញ្ហាប្រឈម និងទស្សនៈវិស័យរបស់វិស័យធានារ៉ាប់រង”
Category: news

កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមប្រឹក្សា អ.ស.ហ. (អាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ) លើកទី១ អាណត្តិទី២

នៅព្រឹកថ្ងៃចន្ទ ៤កើត ខែស្រាពណ៍ ឆ្នាំមមី អដ្ឋស័ក ព.ស.២៥៧០ ត្រូវនឹងថ្ងៃទី១៧ ខែសីហា គ.ស.២០២៦ ឯកឧត្តម ប៊ូ ច័ន្ទភីរូ អគ្គនាយកនៃនិយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា (ន.ធ.ក. (និយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងកម្ពុជា)) និងជាសមាជិកក្រុមប្រឹក្សាអាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ (អ.ស.ហ. (អាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ)) បានអញ្ជើញចូលរួមកិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមប្រឹក្សា អ.ស.ហ. (អាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ) លើកទី១ អាណត្តិទី២ ក្រោមអធិបតីភាពដ៏ខ្ពង់ខ្ពស់របស់ ឯកឧត្តមអគ្គបណ្ឌិតសភាចារ្យ អូន ព័ន្ធមុនីរ័ត្ន ឧបនាយករដ្ឋមន្ត្រី រដ្ឋមន្ត្រីក្រសួងសេដ្ឋកិច្ចនិងហិរញ្ញវត្ថុ និងជាប្រធានក្រុមប្រឹក្សា អ.ស.ហ. (អាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ) ដែលបានប្រព្រឹត្តទៅនៅសាលប្រជុំនៃទីស្តីការ អ.ស.ហ. (អាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ)។

Donated IT equipment to Primary School in Kampong Ous Commune
29 April 2024 8:21:53 AM
On the morning of Saturday, 27th April 2024, Insurance Regulator of Cambodia (IRC), donated IT equipments such as desktop computers and printers to Chrey Andet and Phrum Kdol Primary School in Kampong Ous Commune, Ponhea Leu District, Kandal Province for facilitating daily work.

ព័ត៌មានថ្មីៗ
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមប្រឹក្សា អ.ស.ហ. (អាជ្ញាធរសេវាហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនមែនធនាគារ) លើកទី១៦ អាណត្តិទី១
២៨ ធ្នូ ២០២៣ ១១:០០:៣៧ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាស្តីពី “អត្ថប្រយោជន៍នៃការធានារ៉ាប់រងជាកាតព្វកិច្ច”
២៨ ធ្នូ ២០២៣ ៨:០២:៣៧ ព្រឹក
កិច្ចប្រជុំក្រុមការងារអន្តរក្រសួង ដើម្បីអនុវត្តប្រកាសអន្តរក្រសួងស្តីពី កាតព្វកិច្ចធានារ៉ាប់រង លើកទី៤
២៧ ធ្នូ ២០២៣ ៣:០៥:៤៧ ល្ងាច
សិក្ខាសាលាផ្សព្វផ្សាយស្តីពី "នីតិវិធីនៃការទទួល និងដោះស្រាយបណ្តឹងធានារ៉ាប់រង" នៅខេត្តក្រចេះ
២៦ ធ្នូ ២០២៣ ៣:១២:៤១ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំពិគ្រោះយោបល់លើសេចក្តីព្រាងប្រកាសស្ដីពី “គោលការណ៍ណែនាំអំពីការធានារ៉ាប់រងបន្ត”
២២ ធ្នូ ២០២៣ ៣:៤៨:៣៩ ល្ងាច
ពិធីសំណេះ​សំណាលក្រុមនិស្សិតជ័យលាភីអាហាររូបករណ៍រដ្ឋាភិបាលអូស្ត្រាលី
១៤ ធ្នូ ២០២៣ ១:៥៧:០១ ល្ងាច
កិច្ចប្រជុំពិនិត្យ និងពិភាក្សាលើខ្លឹមសារសេចក្តីព្រាងប្រកាស និងអនុក្រឹត្យជាមួយក្រសួងយុត្តិធម៌
១៣ ធ្នូ ២០២៣ ១១:៣៧:៤៤ ព្រឹក
កិច្ចប្រជុំនិយ័តករធានារ៉ាប់រងអាស៊ាន លើកទី២៦ (26th AIRM)

What is “Catastrophic Risk”​?
Catastrophic Risk is the risk that a single
event of major magnitude leads to a
significantly higher than usual number
and/or amount of claims on an insurer.
Sponsored by
Prepared by: ﻿Insurance Regulator of Cambodia
Source: Glossary of Insurance by Insurance Regulator of Cambodia (2022)

text:
at Department of Business Administration of Zaman University in Cambodia in 2013.
Trainings:
Throughout her career as Deputy Director of the Insurance and Pension Department of the
General Department of Financial Industry of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, Dr.
Sovathana has joint several capacity building such as Seminar on “Emerging Insurance
Market” by KLIA, GIAK, FSS in Korea, “Global Leadership in Financial Supervision”,
Toronto Center International Program for Insurance and Pension Supervisor at the
Executive Learning Center of the Schulich School of Business, York University in Canada
and the 41st Seminar on “Non-Life Insurance and Risk Management in Japan”, General
Course, GIAJ and ISJ, Japan in 2014. She attended the OLIS Seminar on ‘Risk
Management” in Japan in 2015, the 12 Seminar on Improvement of Insurance
Supervision at the Financial Service Agency (FSA) in Japan, The International Insurance
Regulation and Supervision Seminar on “Market Conduct Examination and Financial
Technology in Insurance” in Thailand and the Academy on Social Security, ITC-ILO
Training Center in Turin, Italy in 2016. In 2017, she attended the 27 Seminar on
“Strategy for Sustainable Growth of Non-Life Insurance Companies”, Advanced Course,
GIAJ and ISJ in Japan.
Academic Institution Membership:
Dr. Sovathana was member of the Research Institute of Economics and Business
Administration (RIEB) of Kobe University in Japan from 2003 to 2005 and was member of
the Japan Academy of International Business Studies (JAIBS) and the Academic
Association for Organizational Science in Japan from 2005 to 2008 respectively.
Thesis and Dissertation:
Dr. Sovathana has conducted her research on “Competitive Strategy of GSM Mobile Phone
Companies in Cambodia” for her Master thesis in 2005 and completed the “Comparative
Study of Mobile Phone Diffusion in Cambodia, Lao PDR, and Vietnam” for her Doctoral
dissertation in 2008.
Award and other Achievements:
At the age of 11, Sovathana was selected to represent the Cambodian children in the
“Children’s Right” program at the United Nations Head Quarter in New York in 1989 and
start her journey around the world. In 1996, she received the Canadian scholarship
through “Programme Canadien de Bourses de la Francophonie (PCBF)’ for her
undergraduate studies and received the Japanese government scholarship (Monbukagakusho) in
2001 for her graduate studies. During her career at the Ministry of Economy and Finance,
she received the Honor of “Silver Medal” for her contribution to her role as Deputy Director
of Insurance and Pension Department of the Financial Industry General Department of
the Ministry of Economy and Finance from the Royal Government of Cambodia.

text:
Ms. Tan Linna is the Deputy Director General of the Insurance Regulator of
Cambodia at the Non-Banking Financial Services Authority (NBFSA). She has
20 years of professional experience in supervision, regulations, and development
of insurance, financial management, and institutional leadership in Cambodia’s
financial sector especially in insurance sector.
In her current role, she contributes to the development and implementation of
regulatory frameworks for the insurance industry, including policies related to
insurance supervision, market conduct development, consumer protection, solven-
cy management, and investment oversight. She also provides strategic leadership
insupervising licensed insurance institutions to ensure compliance with Cambodian
laws and prudential standards while promoting the sustainable growth of the
insurance sector.
Recognized for her strong leadership and strategic vision, Ms. Linna has extensive
experience in building effective teams, strengthening regulatory frameworks,
and fostering collaboration between government institutions and financial sector
stakeholders. in addition to this, she served for two years experience in senior
leadership positions ranging from CFO to DCEO. During this period, she contributed
to setting up the bank’s financial management framework, operational systems,
and governance structures, as well as supporting the bank’s early-stage strategic
and operational development.
She has participated in executive programs at the University of California,Berkeley,
and recently completed a Master of Administration at Nanyang Technological
University in Singapore. She also holds a Master of Business Administration in
Finance and a Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration in Accounting from
the National University of Management, Cambodia.

Source file: https://object.irc.gov.kh/irc-public/upload/2024/1afe2ba9-1e64-43e6-a5fc-ab7d5a735da8.pdf

តើ "ការធានារ៉ាប់រងមានកាលកំណត់"
មានន័យដូចម្ដេច ?
ការធានារ៉ា ប់រងមានកាលកំណត់​គឺជាការធានារ៉ា ប់រងអាយុ
ជីវិតនៅពេលដែលអ្នកត្រូវបានធានារ៉ា ប់រងបានស្លា ប់នៅ
ក្នុងរយៈពេលដែលបានកំណត់ជាក់លាក់ណាមួយ ដូចជា
៥​(ប្រាំ)​ឆ្នាំ ឬ១០​(​ដប់)​ឆ្នាំ ឬស្លា ប់នៅមុនអាយុដែល
បានកំណត់ទុកដោយផ្ដល់ផលប្រយោជន៍ទៅឱ្យអ្នកទទួល-
ផលដូចបានកំណត់ក្នុងកិច្ចសន្យានោះ។ ប្រសិនបើអ្នក
ត្រូវបានធានារ៉ា ប់រងនៅមានជីវិតបន្ទា ប់ពីរយៈពេលដែល
បានកំណត់ទុកក្នុងកិច្ចសន្យានោះអ្នកទទួលផលពុំអាច
ទទួលផលប្រយោជន៍ពីការធានារ៉ា ប់រងនេះឡើយ។
សហការឧបត្ថម្ភដោយ៖
រៀបចំដោយ៖ និយ័តករធានារ៉ា ប់រងកម្ពុ ជា
ប្រភព៖ សទ្ទា នុក្រមធានារ៉ា ប់រង រៀបចំដោយ និយ័តករធានារ៉ា ប់រងកម្ពុជា (គ.ស. ២០២២)

No.024.43: What is "Liability Insurance" ? - 44a16124-9a97-462c-8fe2-a2dda376ce57.pdf
Source file: https://object.irc.gov.kh/irc-public/upload/2024/44a16124-9a97-462c-8fe2-a2dda376ce57.pdf

What​is “ Liability Insurance ”​?
Liability Insurance is an insurance contract
covering an indemnity amount whereby the
insured is obliged to pay to a third party who
is physically injured or deceased,​or whose
property is damaged by the acts of the insured
or any activities under the responsibility of the
insured. Types of liability​insurance products
include motor vehicle liability insurance,​
construction site liability insurance, and
passenger transportation liability insurance.
Sponsored by
Prepared by: ﻿Insurance Regulator of Cambodia
Source: Glossary of Insurance by Insurance Regulator of Cambodia (2022)

Unofficial Translation by the Insurance Regulator of Cambodia (IRC)

- Insured refers to a natural person or legal entity who purchases an insurance policy, and in some cases can be both the owner of insurance policy and the insured.
- Beneficiary refers to a third party of a contract that has been determined as having legal rights in receiving any benefits related to only life insurance.
- Insurance applicant refers to a natural person or legal entity who may become an insured in the future and has filled and signed a written application form of the insurance company describing personal circumstances.
- Motor Vehicle refers to vehicles which are powered by the engine to move either in water or on land.

Chapter 2
Competent Authority

Article 5.-
The Ministry of Economy and Finance shall be competent in issuing regulations, managing and supervising the conduct of insurance businesses in accordance with this Law.

Article 6.-
The Ministry of Economy and Finance shall be competent in establishing and managing the insurance development fund to enhance the development, support and promotion of dissemination of insurance benefits to the public.

Chapter 3
Insurance Contract
Section 1
General Procedure

Article 7.-
An Insurance, whether life insurance or general insurance, which is beneficial to the natural person or legal entity to insure against any risks, shall be made only with an insurance company that has been licensed to operate its insurance business in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

5

[Page 6]
Unofficial Translation by the Insurance Regulator of Cambodia (IRC)

Article 8._

Insurance contract shall clearly stipulate the relation between rights and duties of the insured person and the insurance company. The insurance contract shall be made in Khmer language and shall be signed and/or affixed with a thumbprint by both parties.

Article 9._

In process of making an insurance contract, the insured person and the insurance company shall respect the principles of good faith, mutual benefits, and unanimity through negotiation and shall not harm the public interests.

Article 10._

Insurance company is obligated to clearly explain to an insured the terms and conditions of insurance contract and the contents of the insurance policy which is attached with the certificate of insurance and/or other relevant documents.

Article 11._

text:
General insurance is an insurance contract made by the insured and the insurance company
whereby the payment of the insurance premium shall be made to cover risks to property, liability
and health. Types of general insurance products include property insurance, liability insurance,
and health insurance.

Property insurance is an insurance contract whereby an indemnity is paid to the insured when
the property of that person is damaged, lost or destroyed by a risk insured against. The indemnity
to be paid by the insurance company to the insured shall not exceed the value of an object declared
at the time of the conclusion of the insurance contract unless agreed otherwise. Property which is
the subject of property insurance includes buildings, vessels, etc.

Liability insurance is an insurance contract covering an indemnity amount whereby the
insured is obliged to pay to a third party who is physically injured or deceased, or whose property
is damaged by the acts of the insured or any activities under the responsibility of the insured. Types
of liability insurance products include motor vehicle liability insurance, construction site liability
insurance, and passenger transportation liability insurance.

Section 4

Reinsurance

Article 32._

Reinsurance is an insurance operation where a ceding insurance company is insured by other reinsurance company which is wholly or partially reinsures of the insured risks under an insurance contract.

In such case of reinsurance, the ceding insurance company shall remain responsible for the insured.

Chapter 4

Types of Compulsory Insurance

Section 1

Motor Vehicle Liability Insurance

Article 33._

A natural person or legal entity, who is the owner of a motor vehicle, conducting business in the Kingdom of Cambodia shall have an insurance for his/her motor vehicle from an insurance company for the liability of all damages caused to any third party resulting from the operation of his/her motor vehicle, including all types of trailers.

Such insurance is not only effective for motor vehicle owners but also for drivers and motor vehicle maintainers.

text:
ព្រះរាជាណាចព្ររម្ពុជា
ជាតិ សាសនា ព្រះម្ហារសព្ត
rrr2sss
ជីវព្រវតត ិសង្ខេរ
រ-រ័ត៌មានផ្ទាល់ខ្ លួន
គោត្តនាម និងនាម ទូច គម៉េងគេង ជាអក្សរឡាតាំង TOUCH MENGLENG គេទ ប្រុស
ថ្ងៃខែឆ្នាំក្ាំគ ើត្ ១៥ វិចិ ឆកា ១៩៩២ ជនជាត្ិ ខែែ រ សញ្ជាត្ិខែែ រ
ទីក្ខនែងក្ាំគ ើត្ េូមិសួងលិច ឃាំសួងប្សុក្ត្បូងឃែុ ាំ គែត្តក្ាំពង់ចាម (រចចុរបននគែត្ត្បូងឃែុ ាំ)
ទូរស័ពទ ០១៧ ៧១១ ៩១១
អីខម៉េល menglengtouch.irc@gmail.com/touch.mengleng@gmail.com
ខ្-ព្រវតតិការសិរា
២០១៩-២០២០ ររិញ្ជារប្ត្ជាន់ែពស់ខននក្ហិរញ្ាវត្ថុ ពីសាក្ល វិទលល័ Nottingham
Trent University ចប្ក្េពអង់គលែស គប្កាមអាហារូរក្រ ៍ Chevening
Scholarship
២០១១-២០១៥ ររិញ្ជារប្ត្អក្សរសាស្រសតអង់គលែស ពីសាក្ល វិទលល័ េូមិនទេនាំគព
២០១០-២០១៤ ររិញ្ជារប្ត្ វិទលសាស្រសតគសឋកក្ិចច ពីសាក្ល វិទលល័ េូមិនទនីត្ិសាស្រសត
និង វិទលសាស្រសតគសឋកក្ិចច
គ-ព្រវតតិការងារ
សីហា ២០២១-រចចុរបនន ប្រធាននា ក្ដ្ឋកន នា ក្ដ្ឋកនអេិវឌ្ឍន៍ទីនារ, និ ័ត្ក្រធានារ៉ា រ់រង
ក្មពុជា, អាជាាធរគសវាហិរញ្ាវត្ថុមិនខមនធនាោរ
ក្ញ្ជា ២០១៥-សីហា២០២១ មស្រនតី ការិយាល័ គសាធន, នា ក្ដ្ឋកនធានារ៉ា រ់រងនិងគសាធន, អលគ-
នា ក្ដ្ឋកនឧសាហក្មែហិរញ្ាវត្ថុ, ប្ក្សួងគសឋកក្ិចច និងហិរញ្ាវត្ថុ
មីនា ២០១៥-ត្លា២០១៥ ប្លូរគប្ងៀនភាសាអង់គលែសគប្ៅគ ៉េ ង សាលាគរៀន American Bridge
International School
ត្លា ២០១៤-ឧសភា២០១៥ ជាំនួ ការអនក្ប្សាវប្ជាវ វិទលសាថនប្សាវប្ជាវ និងអេិវឌ្ឍន៍ប្ត្ីទឹក្សារ
(IFReDI), រឋកបាលជលនល(FiA), ប្ក្សួងក្សិក្មែ រកាាប្រ ់ និង
គនសាទ (MAFF)
មីនា២០១៤-ត្លា២០១៤ អនក្រក្ខប្រឯក្សារពីភាសារអង់គលែស គៅ ភាសាខែែ រ គៅ Raijing
Media Inc.
ឃ-ការព្សាវព្ជាវ
ឧសភា ២០២០ Merger and Acquisition Analysis
Provide a detailed analysis of an M&A deal involving Berry
Global Group, Inc. (Acquire) acquiring RPC Group Plc
(Target). This analysis consists of cumulative abnormal
return, abnormal buy-and-hold return, and operating
performance measured by ROA
ក្មភៈ ២០២០ Financial Modeling Report of J Sainsbury Plc.
Develop a financial model to project future cash flow and
share price of J Sainsbury PLC (XLON:SBRY) using Pro-
forma Model. This excel-based model is developed based
on the analysis the last 5 years financial performance of
the company.
មក្រ ២០២០ Shareholder Value Analysis
Provide a detailed analysis of Mitchells and Butlers Plc
using SVA (Shareholder Value Analysis Model) taking into
consideration dividend policy and capital structure of the
company.

ជាលាយលក្ខណ៍អក្សរ ដោយយកភាសាខ្មែរជាគោល។

ទៅក្រុមហ៊ុនធានារ៉ាប់រងដោយផ្ទាល់ឬតាមរយៈអន្តរការីធានារ៉ាប់រង ក្នុងទម្រង់លិខិតអនុសិដ្ឋដោយមាន
ហត្ថលេខានិង/ឬ ស្នាមមេដៃ។ ផ្អែកលើពាក្យស្នើសុំប្រតិប័ទន៍នេះ ក្រុមហ៊ុនធានារ៉ាប់រងត្រូវធ្វើការសិក្សានិង
ត្រួតពិនិត្យ។ ក្នុងករណីដែលក្រុមហ៊ុនធានារ៉ាប់រងឯកភាពលើពាក្យស្នើសុំ ក្រុមហ៊ុនធានារ៉ាប់រងអាចចេញ
បណ្ណសន្យារ៉ាប់រងជូនបាន។

នៅក្នុងករណីចាំបាច់ឬបន្ទាន់ណាមួយដែលបណ្ណសន្យារ៉ាប់រងមិនទាន់ត្រូវបានចេញ ការធានារ៉ាប់រងអាច
ប្រព្រឹត្តទៅបានដោយការប្រើប្រាស់ “កំណត់សំអាង” ជាបណ្តោះអាសន្ន។

text:
ផលិតផលធានារ៉ាប់រង គឺជាកិច្ចសន្យាធានារ៉ាប់រងដែលដាក់លក់លើទីផ្សារធានារ៉ាប់រង។ គំរូកិច្ចសន្យា
ធានារ៉ាប់រងទាំងអស់ដែលហៅថា ផលិតផលធានារ៉ាប់រង ត្រូវមានការអនុញ្ញាតពី **ធ.ធ.ក.** មុននឹងដាក់លក់នៅ
លើទីផ្សារធានារ៉ាប់រង។

**២. អានុភាពនៃការធានារ៉ាប់រង**

**មាត្រា១៨ .-**

ការធានារ៉ាប់រងមានប្រសិទ្ធភាពចាប់ពីកាលបរិច្ឆេទ ដែលអ្នកត្រូវបានធានារ៉ាប់រងបានបង់បុព្វលាភ
ធានារ៉ាប់រងតាមកាលកំណត់ក្នុងកិច្ចសន្យាធានារ៉ាប់រង។

ទំព័រ ៧

[Page 8]
ក្នុងករណីក្រុមហ៊ុនធានារ៉ាប់រងមិនបានកំណត់កាលបរិច្ឆេទអានុភាពនៃការធានាឬកាលបរិច្ឆេទបង់
បុព្វលាភធានារ៉ាប់រងនៅក្នុងឯកសារណាមួយនៃកិច្ចសន្យាធានារ៉ាប់រង កាលបរិច្ឆេទដែលអ្នកត្រូវបានធានារ៉ាប់រង
បានបង់បុព្វលាភធានារ៉ាប់រងត្រូវសន្មតថាជាកាលបរិច្ឆេទនៃអានុភាពការធានារ៉ាប់រង។

អ្នកត្រូវបានធានារ៉ាប់រងមានសិទ្ធិប្រើប្រាស់កាលបរិច្ឆេទនៃបង្កាន់ដៃបង់បុព្វលាភធានារ៉ាប់រង ជាភស្តុតាង
បញ្ជាក់ពីកាលបរិច្ឆេទនៃអានុភាពការធានារ៉ាប់រង។

**៣. កាតព្វកិច្ចរបស់អ្នកត្រូវបានធានារ៉ាប់រង**

**មាត្រា១៩ .-**

អ្នកត្រូវបានធានារ៉ាប់រង មានកាតព្វកិច្ចដូចតទៅ៖

**១_** ផ្តល់ព័ត៌មានផ្ទាល់មាត់និង/ឬឯកសារលាយលក្ខណ៍អក្សរដោយពិស្តារ ច្បាស់លាស់ប្រកបដោយ
ភាពស្មោះត្រង់ ទៅឱ្យក្រុមហ៊ុនធានារ៉ាប់រងឬអន្តរការីធានារ៉ាប់រង។

**២_** បង់បុព្វលាភធានារ៉ាប់រង ដោយអនុលោមទៅតាមតារាងនៃការបង់បុព្វលាភធានារ៉ាប់រងរបស់អ្នក
ត្រូវបានធានារ៉ាប់រងនីមួយៗ។ ការបង់បុព្វលាភធានារ៉ាប់រង គឺជាកាតព្វកិច្ចចម្បងរបស់អ្នកត្រូវ
បានធានារ៉ាប់រង។ នៅក្នុងការបង់បុព្វលាភធានារ៉ាប់រងនេះ អ្នកត្រូវបានធានារ៉ាប់រងមានសិទ្ធិ
ចរចាជាមួយក្រុមហ៊ុនធានារ៉ាប់រង ដើម្បីសម្រេចយកការបង់បុព្វលាភធានារ៉ាប់រងសរុបឬបង់
ជាដំណាក់កាល។

Source file: https://object.irc.gov.kh/irc-public/upload/2024/bd4b1f96-d704-40c9-9ece-e69f9d7ba1a4.pdf

តើ "ការធានារ៉ាប់រងមានកាលកំណត់"
មានន័យដូចម្ដេច ?
ការធានារ៉ា ប់រងមានកាលកំណត់​គឺជាការធានារ៉ា ប់រងអាយុ
ជីវិតនៅពេលដែលអ្នកត្រូវបានធានារ៉ា ប់រងបានស្លា ប់នៅ
ក្នុងរយៈពេលដែលបានកំណត់ជាក់លាក់ណាមួយ ដូចជា
៥​(ប្រាំ)​ឆ្នាំ ឬ១០​(​ដប់)​ឆ្នាំ ឬស្លា ប់នៅមុនអាយុដែល
បានកំណត់ទុកដោយផ្ដល់ផលប្រយោជន៍ទៅឱ្យអ្នកទទួល-
ផលដូចបានកំណត់ក្នុងកិច្ចសន្យានោះ។ ប្រសិនបើអ្នក
ត្រូវបានធានារ៉ា ប់រងនៅមានជីវិតបន្ទា ប់ពីរយៈពេលដែល
បានកំណត់ទុកក្នុងកិច្ចសន្យានោះអ្នកទទួលផលពុំអាច
ទទួលផលប្រយោជន៍ពីការធានារ៉ា ប់រងនេះឡើយ។
សហការឧបត្ថម្ភដោយ៖
រៀបចំដោយ៖ និយ័តករធានារ៉ា ប់រងកម្ពុ ជា
ប្រភព៖ សទ្ទា នុក្រមធានារ៉ា ប់រង រៀបចំដោយ និយ័តករធានារ៉ា ប់រងកម្ពុជា (គ.ស. ២០២២)

021 is an important starting point for the non-banking
financial services sector and also a new turning point for
the development of the insurance sector in Cambodia.
These are the newly fruitful achievements resulting from the
efforts of the Royal Government of Cambodia under the wise
leadership and long-term vision of Samdech Akka Moha
Sena Padei Techo HUN Sen, Prime Minister of the Kingdom
of Cambodia, in diversifying the economy by promoting the
development and diversification of banking and non-banking
financial products and services. Despite the rapid growth, the
non-banking financial sector, which is still facing several challenges, has to be more focused,
reviewed, and strengthened in order to continuously contribute as a new and robust source of
Cambodian economic growth.
In the matter of prolonging the COVID-19 crisis, building resilience, ensuring stability, and
strengthening the capability of the financial system are the top priority of the Royal Government
of Cambodia in 2021 and beyond by continuing to diversify financial products and develop
additional financial system infrastructure, especially financial technology (FinTech), to adapt and
respond effectively to the changes of economic and social conditions and crisis in the future.
However, the COVID-19 crisis and the potential of digital transition, which are separated issues,
have become complementary catalysts to further accelerate Cambodia's adoption of financial
technology to drive the non-banking financial services sector to have inclusive growth. The
adoption and digitalization in the non-banking financial services sector will bring opportunities for
new sources of growth, increase economic productivity, create jobs, and reduce poverty and social
inequality.
In the context of the rapid growth of digital technology, insurance technology (InsurTech), which
Page 3
is a part of the financial technology system, is having a huge impact on the insurance sector, both
regionally and internationally, and it is beginning to gradually impact on the Cambodian market
which is strongly required more competitiveness and innovation of the private sector, as well as
the effective work of the Insurance Regulator of Cambodia in regulating and supervising the
insurance institutions’ business activities and financial position, to ensure the soundness of the
insurance sector in Cambodia.

insurance sector in Cambodia, Insurance Regulator of Cambodia (IRC) has formulated a
“Cambodia Strategic Development Plan for Insurance Sector 2021-2030” with a detailed key
action plan for implemention covering the institutional framwork, technical framwork, regulatory
framwork, market conduct framwork and cooperation framework. In addition, numerous
achievements were also accomplished in 2021, such as issuing of a guideline for insurance agent
professional training, amendingt some regulations, raising public awareness, promoting and
encouraging the development of new insurance products, strengthening risk-based supervision

2.1. Institutional Structure
Under the Law on the Organization and Functioning of the Non-Bank Financial Services Authority, Page 6
which was officially promulgated by Royal Decree No. NS/RKM/0121/003, dated January 16, 2021,
Non-Bank Financial Services Authority (abbreviated as FSA), has been established to
independently perform its functions in regulating and supervising non-banking financial sectors
including insurance and private pension sector, securities and exchange sector, social security
sector, trust sector, accounting and auditing sector, and real estate business and pawnshop sector,
in order to ensure the effectiveness in the monitoring, supervising and developing non-banking
financial sectors, as well as promoting the development and the utilization of financial technology
in the non-banking financial sectors in Cambodia

PART III: INSURANCE MARKET FRAMEWORK
r () s
3.1. Insurance Institutions
3.1.1. Insurance Companies Page 15
From 2017 to present, the Cambodian insurance sector has grown rapidly, with the number of
direct insurers increasing from 26 in 2017 to 39 in 2021. Despite the COVID-19 crisis, as of the
end of 2021, IRC had granted business licenses to 18 general insurance companies, 14 life
insurance companies, and 7 micro-insurance companies. These companies include 23 foreign
companies, 15 local companies, and one joint-venture company.
Currently, the Cambodian insurance market has only one reinsurance company, namely
“Cambodia Re” which has evolved from a state-owned company to a joint-venture company with
80% state-owned shares and has been continually privatized to only 60.21% state-owned shares.

3.1.2. Insurance Intermediaries
Insurance intermediaries, including insurance brokers and insurance agents, have played a key role Page 17
in the Cambodian insurance sector in distributing insurance products more widely and bringing
insurance products closer to customers. To support the growth of the insurance sector by
strengthening and expanding the social safety net, the number of insurance intermediaries had
increased from 28 in 2017 to 43 in 2021. As of the end of 2021, the insurance market had 26
insurance agents and 17 insurance brokers.

3.2. Insurance Market
The spread of the COVID-19 crisis had placed severe pressure on the sources of Cambodia's Page 18
economic growth as reflected through the negative growth of 3.1% in the Cambodian economy in
2020, and recovering back to a positive growth of 3% in 2021 via the implementation of timely
preventive measures by the Royal Government of Cambodia. Even though in the context of the
COVID-19 crisis, Cambodia's insurance market has continued significantly boosting and
maintaining a strong financial position with a positive growth of approximately 8% in 2020 and
10% in 2021.
3.2.1. Insurance Premium
Gross Insurance premium increased significantly from USD153 million in 2017 to approximately
USD300 million in 2021. It has an average growth of about 20% over the last five years.
Meanwhile, the net insurance premium in 2021 increased to USD 217 million with a retention ratio
of more than 70% which indicates that the insurance companies would have adequate underwriting
capacity and robust financial strength to mitigate most risk themselves.

Insurance penetration and insurance density are the key indicators used to assess the level of
Page 19
development of insurance sector in a country. An insurance penetration rate is calculated by
dividing gross premium of an insurance market by gross domestic product (GDP) of a country. An
insurance density is calculated by dividing gross premium of an insurance market by a population
of a country resulting in an amount per capita.
The penetration rate of Cambodia’s insurance market increased from 0.69% in 2017 to 1.11% in
2021 while the insurance density expanded from USD10.06 per capita in 2017 to USD18.75 per
capita in 2021. Even though, Cambodia’s insurance market is significantly growing, its penetration
rate and insurance density still remain very low compared to the region.

Insurance companies use various product-distribution channels such as insurance brokers,
insurance agents, bancassurance and sale staffs. In 2021, bancassurance was one of the distribution

followed by companies’ sale staff at about 23%. Insurance agents sold insurance brokers sold 20%
and 10% accordingly. It is noted that the increase in sale of insurance products via banks is the
effort of National Bank of Cambodia and Insurance Regulator of Cambodia to streamline financial
services under the Royal Government’s strategic plan for financial inclusion.

a. General Insurance Products

such as vehicles, fire, marine, engineering, personal accidents, health, and others. In 2021, general

took the highest market share of about 30.4% of the total gross premium followed by health insurance
at about 21.9%, the motor insurance at about 17.5% and marine insurance, which accounted for
only 3.4% of the total gross premium.

3.2.3. Insurance Claims Incurred
Page 25
Over the last five years, the figure of insurance claims incurred in the general and micro insurance
market have significantly changed. The highest claims incurred in 2019 at USD13.85 million with
the claim ratio of 33% and at USD13.19 million with the claim ratio of 31% in 2020. Whereas in
2021, the insurance claim incurred in these two markets dropped to only USD11.97 million with
the claim ratio of 26%.
On the other hand, the figure of insurance claims incurred in Cambodia’s life insurance market
had also increased significantly, from USD26.2 million in 2017 to USD86.5 million in 2021, with
an average increase of about 35% over the last 5 years.

3.2.4. Annual Profits/Losses
a. Underwriting Profit/Loss Page 26
Despite the significant increase in the amount of insurance claims incurred, insurance companies
are still making profits from their business operations with increase from year to year. In fact,
profits from insurance underwriting increased from USD35.1 million in 2017 to USD60.8 million

3.2.5. Assets of Insurance Market

economy. For instance, the assets of Cambodia’s insurance market increased from USD286 million in

insurance companies possessed the largest share of total assets which constantly increased to USD552
million in 2021. Also, the assets of general insurance companies remarkably increased by moving up
from USD139 million in 2017 to USD294 million in 2021, whereas the assets of micro-insurance market
decreased from USD8 million to USD5 million in 2021.

annual growth rate of 53% for the last five years. Meanwhile, the total liabilities increased from
USD126 million in 2017 to USD481 million in 2021 with an annual growth rate of 40% over the

3.3. Insurance Professional Training
Insurance professional training plays a role in bridging insurer and insured that energetically
contributes to promote insurance market growth of Cambodia. However, since the insurance
activities has resumed in late 80s in Cambodia, trainings for insurance professional have not
been officially organized. Furthermore, there have not been any courses on insurance conducted
at higher education level. Since 2005, some general insurance companies have built up their
employees’ capacity by providing online courses on insurance in cooperation with other
insurance schools in the region such as Malaysian Insurance Institute (MII) and School of
Insurance Singapore etc. As a result, there were only few candidates who completed the courses.
Nowadays, Cambodia Reinsurance Co., in cooperation with Malaysian Insurance Institute has
been also providing short training courses to its partner insurance companies’ staffs as well as
others related institutions’. However, the result of the training was still unsatisfactory.
From 2012 as the year of introduction of life insurance into Cambodia market, life insurers have
internally been organizing professional trainings for their agents and sale staff focusing on their
own products. In order to strengthen professional capacity of the market, especially for insurance
agencies, IRC has recently issued the Instruction No. 002 IRC/SN dated 27 August, 2021 on
professional training for Insurance agents in the purpose of issuing a common curriculum to be
Page 32
applied for all insurers conducting insurance agent professional training courses in the Kingdom
of Cambodia. The instruction has guided all insurers to provide two courses of trainings: (1)
basic training course consists of 4 subjects and 8 hours for anyone wishes to join a career in
insurance agent profession, and (2) specialized training course for who has completed the basic
course and wishes to be an insurance agent of a company. Also, the instruction guides insurers
to seek prior approval from IRC on the arrangement of any courses such curriculum, training
materials, teaching methodology, examination procedure, and sampled certificate of completion
and the list of responsible persons for the training. By the end of 2021, IRC approved 20 training
courses provided by 4 general insurance companies, 11 life insurance companies and 5 micro
insurance companies.
Besides that, some companies further provided their staff with various training courses or online
training courses on specific topics such as Insurance Compliance Principle and Customer Service
as well as risk management for life insurance which was conducted in cooperation with the Life
Office Management Association (LOMA) of the United States of America.
Noticeably, the knowledge and skill on professional insurance has been stringently developed
and it is significantly contributing to the growth of insurance market, IRC has set out an
ambitious action plan under a clear human resource development framework of “Cambodia
Strategic Development Plan for Insurance Sector 2021-2030” as fellows:
- Continuously promote insurance professional trainings which have to be formally
organized step by step based on IRC’s available financial resources and the actual
needs of the market. In addition, IRC will fully support the Insurance Association of
Cambodia in producing a standard material for the basic training course. Moreover,
IRC will support and encourage the Association to conduct trainings for trainers on
the standard material;
- Cooperate with relevant ministries to introduce the basic and specialized courses on
insurance in curriculum at higher education;
Page 33
- Cooperate with the Insurance Association of Cambodia to study and design training
course for insurance intermediary professionals;
- Conduct a feasibility study on an establishment of “insurance school or the national
institute of insurance” towards setting up plan;
- Review regulations on licensing or intermediaries’ registration to incorporate the
outcomes of the organization of formal training courses on insurance profession and
to encourage for the formation of Cambodia’s Insurance Broker Association.
3.4. Compulsory Insurance
Compulsory insurance is an insurance contract, which is obliged by a law to any natural or legal
persons. Under the law on insurance, three compulsory insurance contracts have been put into
force such as: 1) compulsory insurance for construction site, 2) compulsory insurance of passenger
transport and 3) compulsory motor vehicle or third-party liability insurance. To implement these
compulsory insurances, the Royal Government has issued more regulations such as:
• Sub-Decree on Insurance No. 275 ANKR.BK Phnom Penh, December 30, 2021, Chapter
4, on Types of Compulsory Insurance
• Inter-Ministerial Prakas No. 655 PRK.SHV.DNS.MPH, Phnom Penh 16 October 2002 on
Compulsory Insurance for Construction site
• Inter-Ministerial Prakas No. 654 PRK.SHV.SK.MPH, Phnom Penh 16 October 2002 on
Compulsory Insurance of Passenger Transport
• Inter-Ministerial Prakas No. 653 PRK.SHV.SK.MPH, Phnom Penh 16 October 2002 on
Compulsory Motor Vehicle or Third-Party Liability Insurance
• Prakas No. 002 MEF.PRK Phnom Penh, 03 January 2006 on Motor Vehicle Insurance
Stamp in Compulsory
To strengthen the implementation of compulsory insurance, as the newly established regulator,
IRC has been reviewing and revising all related regulations included inter-ministerial prakas on
compulsory insurance. Furthermore, the working group to implement inter-ministerial prakas on
compulsory insurance has been being revised to update all members from relevant ministries under
the short-term action plan of IRC.
Page 34
a. Compulsory Motor Vehicle or Third-party Liability Insurance
Gross premium of motor vehicle or third-party liability insurance accounted for USD5.2 million
in 2021 which increased by an average of 5.09% with an average growth in number of policies at
7.25% for the last 5 years.

3.5. Raising Public Awareness
Public education and awareness are very important in contributing to the development of the
insurance sector in Cambodia. The low insurance penetration rate and insurance density has
diagnosed that Cambodia’s increase market lacks of public awareness which would definitely be
promoted.
In this regard, in 2021, IRC has set out a number of priority activities, including raising public
awareness of insurance by participating in a series of public talk on National Television of
Cambodia (TVK), to explain to the public about the benefits of insurance, roles and duties of the
Insurance Regulator of Cambodia, law and regulations of Insurance, types of insurance product in
Cambodia’s market and compulsory insurance.

Cambodia" Insurance"
However, IRC has prepared some actions in 2022 to promote the insurance sector through the
Page 37
following activities:
• Organizing dissemination workshops on “Benefits of Compulsory Insurance” in some
target provinces in Cambodia.
• Organizing an insurance knowledge sharing program in the form of publishing short
articles about the insurance sector in Cambodia through various medias such as website
and social network of IRC.
• Producing videos about compulsory insurance for broadcasting on TV, social media, and
the website of Insurance Regulator of Cambodia.
• Organizing consultation meetings with relevant institutions in order to explore the
possibility of including insurance subjects in the undergraduate program.
Page 38
PART IV: COOPERATION
r () s
4.1. Cooperation at National Level
Page 39
❖ Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism and Combating the
Financing of Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction Framework
Insurance Regulator of Cambodia has facilitated the invitation of the insurance companies and
insurance brokers to participate in the workshop on "Proliferation Financing Risk Assessment"
which organized by the Ministry of Interior on October 21, 2021, via video conference. In
addition, in order to strengthen the capacity of the officials and reporting entities under the
jurisdiction of IRC on Law on Combating the Financing of Proliferation of Weapons of Mass
Destruction, IRC has also prepared a training program to be implemented in 2022.
Furthermore, to increase rating on technical compliance related to Anti-Money Laundering and
Combating the Financing of Terrorism and Combating the Financing of Proliferation of Weapons
of Mass Destruction Framework, IRC revised the Prakas and legal documents related to the
licensing of life insurance companies and general insurance companies in accordance with the
recommendations of the Financial Working Group (FATF), requiring a criminal record to be
included in the requirement when applying for a license.
On the other hand, IRC also provided input on the draft of “Directive on Internal Controls for
Reporting Entity” which prepared by the Cambodian Financial Intelligence Unit (CAFIU).
❖ Establishment of an inter-ministerial working group to implement the inter-ministerial
Prakas on Compulsory Insurance
To amend on the Prakas No.751 MEF.PRK Phnom Penh, September 25, 2020 on “Establishment
of an inter-ministerial working group to implement the inter-ministerial Prakas on Compulsory
Insurance”, the Research, Training, and Cooperation Department of the Insurance Regulator of
Cambodia has conducted 03 internal meetings in 2021 to discuss on the adjustment of the
composition, roles and responsibilities of the Inter-Ministerial Working Group in the Prakas.
Page 40
❖ The Meeting of National Transit Transport Coordinating Committees (NTTCC)
The IRC attended the Meeting of National Transit Transport Coordinating Committees on
November 26, 2021. The meeting was conducted in order to discuss on a brief report on
implementation of cross-border transport agreements including Bilateral Agreement, Cambodia-
Laos-Vietnam (CLV) Tripartite Agreement, Greater Mekong Sub-region Cross-Border Transport
Agreement (GMS-CBTA) and ASEAN Transport Facilitation Agreement and Memorandum of
Understanding (MOU) on the increase the quota of vehicles transporting through Cambodia-
Vietnam by reviewing MOU’s final draft after being revised by Vietnam.
Image 33: The Meeting of National Transit Transport Coordinating Committees (NTTCC)
4.2. Cooperation at International Level
❖ ASEAN Insurance Regulators Meeting Page 41
The 24th ASEAN Insurance Regulators Meeting is an annual forum for insurance regulators from
all ASEAN member countries to share ideas and information related to the latest developments in
the insurance sector in the region. This meeting was held from 27th-28th October 2021 virtually
and chaired by the representative of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) with the
participation from all ASEAN member countries. Cambodian delegation, led by H.E. Bou
Chanphirou, Director General of IRC also joined the meeting.
Image 34: 24th ASEAN Insurance Regulators Meeting
Image 35: AIRM-AIC Joint Plenary Meeting
❖ ASEAN Disaster Risk and Financing and Insurance - Phase II (ADRFI - 2)
The IRC has cooperated on the ASEAN Disaster Risk and Financing and Insurance Phase 2, which
Page 42
has three pillars such as Risk Assessment, Risk Advisory and Capacity Building.
Image 36: Bilateral Meeting on ASEAN Disaster Risk and Financing and
Insurance Phase 2 (ADRFI-2) with Nanyang University on November 03, 2021.
Through this cooperation, the IRC has coordinated in providing Cambodia Insurance Exposure
Data and Economic Loss Data to the team in order to support analyzing these data for risk
assessment. In addition, the IRC also coordinated a workshop on Benefits and Uses of Risk
Analysis Toolkit in which ministries and relevant institutions participated.
❖ Organizing IRC’s Regional Forum
To support organizing the showcase event for the Chairmanship of the ASEAN Finance Minister
and Central Bank Governor Meeting in 2022, the IRC has organized a concept note on regional
forum under the topic “Technological Innovations and Impact on Insurance: Challenges,
Opportunities and Way Forward”, scheduled for September 2022.
Page 43
Image 37: The Meeting on Organizing the Showcase Event
❖ The Meeting of the Working Committee on ASEAN Financial Services Liberalization
(WC-FSL)
The IRC assigned representatives to attend the 73rd Meeting of WC-FSL virtually on 6th October
2022 in order to update works progression and discuss on main points such as 1). Discussion on
signing protocol 9 arrangement 2). Discussion on an agenda and relevant points on the 4th ASEAN
SC-FS Caucus and the 4th Meeting of AANZFTA 3). Initiatives for organizing workshops for
capacity building for the ASEAN member countries.
Page 44
PART V: REGULATORY FRAMEWORK
r () s
In 2021, Non-Bank Financial Services Authority, which has competency as regulator in
Page 45
insurance sector, has organized some legal and regulatory frameworks in order to manage and
supervise the insurance business in Cambodia as follows:
❖ Regulations on institutional framework consists of:
- Sub-decree No. 275 ANKr.BK, dated on December 30, 2021, on Insurance replacing
the 2001 Sub-decree on Insurance.
- Prakas No. 005 ASH.Prak dated on October 1, 2021 on the Organization and
Functioning of Departments and Units Under the auspices of the Insurance Regulator
of Cambodia.
- Cambodia Strategic Development Plan for Insurance Sector 2021-2030 approved on
September 15, 2021
Image 39: The 5th Meeting of the 1st Mandate of “The Council of Non-Bank Financial Services
Authority” via virtual video on November 5, 2021 to Review and Discuss on the Draft
Sub-decree on Insurance
Image 40: Consultation Meeting on Draft Sub-decree on Insurance, organized by
Page 46
the Insurance and Pension Department of General Department of Financial
Industry on July 6, 2018.
Image 41: Meeting of the Inter-Ministerial Technical Level on Draft of Sub-decree on
Insurance at the Ministry of Economy and Finance on December 30, 2020.
Page 47
Image 42: Consultation Meeting with Development Partners and the Insurance Association of
Cambodia on the Draft of the 10-year Strategic Development Plan of the Insurance Sector
(2021-2030) via video conference on July 22, 2021
Image 43: Consultation Meeting with Relevant Ministries, Institutions, the Insurance Association of
Cambodia, Insurance Institutions and Accounting and Auditing Firms on the Draft 10-year Strategic
Development Plan of the Insurance Sector (2021-2030) via video conference on July 12, 2021
Page 48
PART VI: CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY
r () s
Page 49
On June 05, 2021, at the call of H.E. Dr. Aun Porn Moniroth, Deputy Prime Minister and
Minister of Economy and Finance and Chairman of the Board of Non-Bank Financial Services
Authority, H.E. Bou Chanphirou, Director General of the Insurance Regulator of Cambodia,
accompanied by the management and officials of the Insurance Regulator of Cambodia, provided
food packages contributed by the insurance institutions to 94 poor families who were affected by
the Covid-19 in Barach Village, Svay Chrum Commune, Khsach Kandal District, Kandal
Province. Each family received a package of food comprising 10kg of rice, 1 box of instant noodles
and 2 boxes of canned fish. In addition, 160kg of rice, 11 boxes of instant noodles, 12 boxes of
canned fish, 5 boxes of fish sauce. Also, 5 boxes of soy sauce were offered to the monks at Barach
Pagoda.
Image 45: Cooperation and Support from the Insurance Institutions in
Cambodia to distribute food packages to the poor on June 05, 2021
On July 09, 2021, at the call of H.E. Dr. Aun Porn Moniroth, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister Page 50
of Economy and Finance, and Chairman of the Board of Non-Bank Financial Services Authority,
H.E. Bou Chanphirou, Director General of the Insurance Regulator of Cambodia, accompanied
by the management and officials of the Insurance Regulator of Cambodia, with participation of
representatives of various insurance institutions, donated food including rice, instant noodles, fish
sauce, soy sauce and soybeans to Khsach Kandal District Administration, Kandal Province through
Mr. Bun Pheng, Governor of Khsach Kandal District to be used during Covid-19 campaign in
Khsach Kandal District, Kandal Province.
Image 46: Cooperation and Support from Insurance Institutions in Cambodia to
distribute food to the poor via Khsach Kandal District Governor on July 09, 2021
On December 18, 2021, the Insurance Regulator of Cambodia and Prudential (Cambodia) Life
Page 51
Insurance Plc. organized a program to distribute sanitation equipment to high schools, primary
schools, kindergartens and health centers in Ream Anderk Commune, Takeo Province.
The program was led by H.E. Bou Chanphirou, Director General of the IRC, accompanied by
some officials of the IRC and with participation of the representatives of Prudential (Cambodia)
Life Assurance Plc, the commune representatives, principals of the schools, commune health
center directors, doctors, teachers and students of Ream Anderk Commune.
Image 47: IRC and Prudential (Cambodia) Life Assurance Plc. donate sanitation equipment to
the educational institutions and health centers in Ream Anderk Commune, Takeo Province
on December 18, 2021
Page 52
PART VII: CONCLUSION
r () s
In 2021, Cambodia, like other countries around the world, was still affected by the protracted
Page 53
effects of the COVID-19 crisis, which had hampered the process of general economic activities.
However, as a result of the Royal Government's efforts, through the introduction of several
measures, Cambodia had been gradually adapting to learning to live in the New Normal, that
encouraged Cambodia to seize new opportunities in the region and the world.
In this regard, “Cambodia Strategic Development Plan for Insurance Sector 2021-2030”
which was approved by the Board of Non-Bank Financial Services Authority on September 15,
2021, together with the fact that COVID-19 situation had become less severe, will create an
opportunity to turn Cambodia’s insurance sector into a strong backbone of Cambodia’s economic
development and social security system. In addition, the COVID-19 crisis also reflected the
growing importance of the insurance sector, by providing additional mechanisms to support social
security sector by reducing the financial burden of individuals, families and society at the time of
loss of life or health problem of an insured family member due to COVID-19.
There are currently 80 insurance institutions operating in Cambodia, with the total assets of
approximately USD 845 million and shareholders’ equities of approximately USD378 million.
The 2021 market has gross insurance premium of approximately USD298 million which
contributes approximately 1.11% to the economy with an insurance density of about $18.75 per
capita.
However, these indicators show that Cambodia’s insurance market still has a huge potential to
grow due to very low penetration rate and insurance density compared to other countries in the
region as well as in the world. It implies that Cambodian insurance market would continue
remarkably growing and attract more investors who would create more jobs in this sector.

TAN LINNA
House # C19, St.Lum, Sk. Boeng Salang, Khan Roesey Keo, Phnom Penh, Cambodia
H/P: 855-12-478887, Email: linnatan9@gmail.com
OVERVIEW
Highly accomplished, results-driven senior accounting and financial management executive
with more than 10 years of progressive experience in finance and operations management
within start-ups. Demonstrated ability to streamline business operations that drive growth
and increase efficiency and bottom-line profit. Strong qualifications in developing and
implementing financial controls and processes in addition to productivity improvements, and
change management. Possesses solid leadership, communication and interpersonal skills to
establish rapport with all levels of staff and management.
CORE QUALIFICATIONS
• Accounting and Financial Management • Operations Efficiencies
• Controllership and Decision Support • Financial Analysis & Reports
• Business Planning and Analysis • Resource Management
• Growth Strategy Development • Strong work ethic
• Performance Measurement • Troubleshooting proficiency
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCES
Deputy Director of Insurance and Pension Department
Ministry of Economic and Finance 2017 to Present
• Overseeing direct daily activities in planning, development of various regarding to the
legal framework of insurance supervision including sub-decree on insurance, micro
insurance and many prakas being developed covering consumer protection and financial
literacy, solvency and investments, code of conduct of intermediary, reinsurance’s treaty.
• Provide leadership, management and direction to the supervision of professional team,
technical and support staff, management review of the responsibilities and work flows
within the Supervision Division in regards to their supervision operations and substantial
future work completed in regards to this area substantial department management
cooperation and guidance.
• Provide strategic recommendations to the senior management and members of the
executive management team.
• Managing the processes for financial forecasting and budgets, and overseeing the
preparation of all financial and activities plan.
• Advising on long-term business and financial planning.
• Establishing and developing relations with senior management, experts, external partners
and stakeholders.
Division Head of Supervision Division, Insurance and Pension Department
Ministry of Economic and Finance 2014 to 2017
• Continuously monitor and analyze the financial solvency of all licensed supervised
entities to make sure that consumers have the services they expect when they need
it and that these entities meet and maintain the requirements set forth in Cambodian
laws, sub-decrees, and prakas;
• Continuously monitor and keep update all financial guideline and operational
procedures has been used by Insurance Institutions in Cambodia.
• Lead the teams to conduct full and focused financial examinations on all licensed
insurance entities to ensure they maintain compliance with Cambodia laws, sub-
decrees, and prakas;
• The review and monitoring of the company’s policy and procedures on internal
controls regarding performing their operations and to make sure that these
operations are handled in a reasonable manner and meet the requirements set forth
in Cambodian laws, sub-decrees, prakas, and best practices;
• The review and confirmation of the company’s financial data collection with the data
submitted to the Department for reasonableness;
• The review and confirmation of the company’s compliance with the orders and
recommendation submitted to the company by the Division in regards to Prudential
Supervision;
• To review and comment on any and all financial data submitted to the other
supervisory departments by an insurance entity for the reason of license renewal,
product approval, or other reasons;
• To review and comment on any Actuary and Auditor request to be added to the list
of approved Actuary or Auditor maintained and published by the insurance
supervisory department.
Officer of Financial Industrial Department
Ministry of Economic and Finance 2007 to 2014.
• To make adequate preparations for on-site inspections after consulting the off-site
examiners.
• To hold discussion with external auditors on issue of concern to the regulator.
• To undertake on-site inspections base on the Manual under conditions of secrecy.
• To ensure compliance to prudential requirements with regards to liquidity, solvency
and profitability.

text:
i
ii
PREFACE
Cambodia, with peace, political stability, and a new normal, under the long-term
vision, wise, robust, and proficient leadership of Samdech Moha Borvor Thipadei
HUN MANET, Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Cambodia, has been continuing to
maintain social and economic growth amid the global crises that brought negative
impacts to national development, caused by the post COVID-19 pandemic, geopolitical
tensions and armed-conflicts in some regions and uncertain trade policy of many
countries in the world. The Royal Government of Cambodia, 7th Legislation of the National
Assembly, had launched the “Pentagonal Strategy-Phase I”, defining 5 key priorities:
People, Road, Water, Electricity, and Technology, as cores for developing an inclusive
and sustainable society and economy. Additionally, the government had subsequently
formulated policies and measures to promptly address the emerging challenges and
foster the development with high flexibility, caution, and responsibility in response to
rapid evolution in the globe, region, and within the country. In 2024, Cambodia’s
economy continued to maintain positive growth around 6%, mainly supported by crucial
factors, including recovery in the garment sector, export-based production, and tourism,
as well as the expansion in new sectors, such as renewable energy and value-added
agricultural businesses, with a focus on financial sector growth, potentially the non-bank
financial sector.
Along with these spectacular achievements and to support the Royal Government
of Cambodia’s 2050 vision in transforming Cambodia into a high-income country,
legislative documents, strategies, and action plans have been continuously launched,
including the non-bank financial sector, which is remarkably growing. The insurance
sector, which is one of the non-bank financial sectors, has been significantly contributing
to addressing financial burdens, protecting people from falling below the poverty line in
times of crisis, and enhancing social responsibility to strengthen the social safety-net and
promote strong economic growth. To boost insurance sector development in Cambodia,
Insurance Regulator of Cambodia (IRC) formulated the “Cambodia Strategic
Development Plan for Insurance Sector 2021-2030”, which was adopted by the
Non-Bank Financial Services Authority Council in 2021, and subsequently launched
various development action plans to support successful implementation of the strategic
plan and to align with the government policies. Until 2025, the strategic plan has been
implemented to mid-term, which is required for a monitoring and evaluation of the
iii
implementation. Therefore, a “Report on the Mid-Term Review of the
Implementation of Cambodia Strategic Development Plan for Insurance Sector
2021-2030”, has been produced by the regulator and demonstrates incredible
outcomes.
Indeed, over the last five years (2021-2024), Cambodia’s insurance market
experienced remarkable growth, as in 2024, the insurance market increased to
approximately USD 357 million of the total gross premium, with insurance policies of
more than 1.7 million policies providing coverage of approximately USD 86 billion. The
market consists of 40 insurance companies (18 general, 14 life, 7 micro, and 1 reinsurance),
20 insurance brokers, 5 loss adjusting companies, 5 actuarial companies, 2 claim
management companies, 45 insurance agent companies, and more than 12 thousand
insurance individual agents. Additionally, as of 2024, the Cambodia’s insurance market
had total assets of over USD 1.2 billion with shareholders’ equity of over USD 449 million.
However, to further develop the sector under the actual context of the Cambodia’s
market and global tendency, the strategic plan, has been updated to “Cambodia
Strategic Development Plan for Insurance Sector 2025-2030”, which is a
roadmap for IRC and relevant stakeholders in developing a sustainable and inclusive
insurance sector of Cambodia by outlining clear development frameworks, such as
(1)Strategic Framework, (2)Insurance Market Framework, (3)Regulatory Framework and
(4)Cooperation and Connectivity Framework. Moreover, key performance indicators have
been reviewed and newly defined to reach the
and , to support the accomplishment
of Cambodia’s 2050 vision.
Taking this opportunity, on behalf of the Council of Non-Bank Financial Services
Authority and myself, I would like to thank and appreciate to ministries, institutions, the
private sector, development partners and all relevant stakeholders for cooperating,
contributing, and implementing the strategic plan and related action plans to promote
the insurance sector development in Cambodia. Furthermore, I would like to express my
high appreciation for the dedicated and proactive efforts of the IRC in diligently carrying
out the function to effectively and efficiently regulate and supervise the insurance sector,
as well as in initiating various initiatives aimed at accelerating market growth and
fostering the sustainable development of the Cambodia’s insurance market.
iv
Finally, I firmly hope that ministries, institutions, and relevant units of the Royal
Government, private institutions, and development partners will continue to support and
collaborate in implementing this strategic plan within their respective jurisdictions, to
achieve the expected outcomes at each phase, building a strong insurance sector and
ensuring the provision of insurance services that are transparent, efficient, and
accountable, aiming at strengthening the social safety-net and promoting sustainable
and inclusive national economic growth.
v
The Pentagonal Strategy-Phase I, the National Strategic Development
Plan 2024–2028, the Financial Sector Development Strategy 2025–2030, and
other key policies of the Royal Government of Cambodia reflect the Government’s strong
commitment and long-term vision to progressively transform the country from a low-
income nation to a middle-income country, and ultimately to achieve high-income status
by 2050. Nevertheless, amid persistent regional and global challenges that continue to
generate high levels of uncertainties, Cambodia’s economy is undergoing a recovery
process with positive momentum, with preliminary estimation indicating that the growth
has not yet returned to its full potential trajectory. In the context of global uncertainty,
which may give rise to elevated risks, the improvement of the business and investment
environment remains a priority to achieve high, sustainable, inclusive, and equitable
economic growth that enhances people’s livelihoods and reduces poverty. Particularly,
the insurance sector, as part of the non-bank financial sector, has been playing an
increasingly important role in ensuring social protection and promoting economic growth
by providing an effective financial protection mechanism to citizens, strengthening
resilience against various shocks, and mobilizing long-term funds for investment through
insurance funds.
Over the past five years (2021–2024), Cambodia’s insurance market has
demonstrated remarkable progress, as in 2024, the insurance market size reached more
than USD 357 million in gross premium, with over 1.7 million insurance policies issued,
providing coverage of approximately USD 86 billion. The Cambodian insurance market
currently comprises of 40 insurance companies (18 general, 14 life, 7 microinsurance,
and 1 reinsurance), 20 insurance brokers, 5 insurance loss adjusting companies, 2
actuarial companies, 2 claim management companies, 45 insurance agent companies,
and approximately more than 1.2 thousand individual insurance agents.
Additionally, as of 2024, the insurance market recorded total assets of approximately
USD 1.2 billion and shareholders’ equity of around USD 449 million. These notable
achievements and progresses are the result of the efforts of the IRC and relevant
institutions in implementing the “Cambodia Strategic Development Plan for

Over the past two decades, anchored by peace, political stability, and social
security, Cambodia has achieved significant progress in macroeconomic and financial
stability, sustainable growth, diversification, resilience, and the inclusive improvement of
people’s livelihoods. Through the Royal Government of Cambodia’s determined efforts,
five core pillars of resilience have been established: institutional resilience,
economic resilience, social and human resilience, financial system resilience,
and environmental and climate resilience. These pillars have enabled Cambodia to
sustain social progress and economic growth, while gradually returning to normalcy
despite having endured the COVID-19 crisis and continuing to face major global
challenges, including geopolitical tensions, armed conflicts in various regions, and
uncertainties in the trade policies of certain countries. These important achievements
have been supported by key actions, including economic integration and participation in
regional and global supply chains; improvements to the investment climate and trade
facilitation to attract new investors; human capital development; and institutional and
governance reforms, in line with the direction and long-term vision set out in the
Pentagonal Strategy-Phase I of the Royal Government of Cambodia.
The insurance sector initially emerged in Cambodia in the late 1980s, when the
country began adopting a free-market economy through market liberalization and the
expansion of international trade. This development created demand for insurance
coverage for the transportation of goods, particularly imports into Cambodia. In the early
1990s, with the presence of a single state-owned enterprise, the National Insurance
Company of Cambodia (CAMINCO), which served both as regulator and operator, the
insurance sector began its gradual development and expansion. The sector further
progressed with the entry of additional general insurance companies starting in 2003. To
date, Cambodia has a total of 40 insurance companies with 38 branch offices nationwide.
In addition, the insurance market includes 60 insurance intermediaries and 8 insurance
support service companies currently operating in the country. The Cambodian insurance
market has maintained steady growth, with an average annual growth rate of
approximately 7% over the past five years, and gross written premiums reaching
approximately USD 357 million in 2024. This growth and development are the result of
the effective implementation of the “Cambodia Strategic Development Plan for
Insurance Sector 2021–2030”, which supports the broader policy agenda of the

Royal Government of Cambodia. Under this strategic framework, the Insurance Regulator
will develop detailed action plans for implementation, including an institutional
development plan for the Insurance Regulator of Cambodia, a rolling three-year action
plan, and annual budget plans.
Nevertheless, amid continuing global challenges that may impact Cambodia’s
economy, the “Insurance Sector Development Strategy 2021–2030”, which
serves as a roadmap for setting clear directions for the development of the insurance
sector, requires updating to the “Insurance Sector Development Strategy 2025–
2030”. This update is necessary to respond to emerging challenges and to ensure the
resilience of Cambodia’s insurance sector.
Cambodia’s insurance sector has been significantly developed under the frameworks
of the Pentagonal Strategy-Phase I, the National Strategic Development Plan
2024–2028, the Financial Sector Development Strategy 2025-2030, and in
particular, the “Cambodia Strategic Development Plan for Insurance Sector
2021–2030”, which serves as a long-term roadmap to ensure sustainable and inclusive
development. However, the implementation of the Cambodia Strategic Development Plan
for Insurance Sector has reached its mid-term phase requiring a comprehensive

Plan for Insurance Sector 2025-2030”, to align with the evolving global context and

2021–2030” and the “Three-Year Rolling Action Plan of the IRC”, both of which

Over the past four years (2021–2024), the size of the insurance market has

The notable growth of Cambodia’s insurance market has been driven by the
expansion and diversification of insurance products to meet market demand, including
property insurance, auto insurance, engineering insurance, MAT insurance, health
insurance, personal accident insurance, liability insurance, and life insurance products
with both protection and savings features. In addition, consumer protection has been
strengthened by the establishment of a clear mechanism to receive and resolve insurance
complaints which has been nationwide disseminated. Insurance literacy has also been
promoted through Cambodia Insurance Day, outreach seminars, public lectures, and
various media campaigns across multiple platforms. Furthermore, improvements in the
professional delivery of insurance services have been supported by the issuance and
implementation of key regulatory instruments, including the Prakas on Procedures for
Receiving and Resolving Insurance Complaints, the Guideline on Professional Training for
Insurance Agents, the Code of Conduct for Insurance Brokers, and the Guideline on the
Prevention of Insurance Fraud.
Nevertheless, Cambodia’s insurance market continues to face several challenges,
including limited implementation of compulsory motor third-party liability insurance and
construction site third-party liability insurance, limited public awareness on insurance
services, and capacity constraints in professional insurance expertise to adequately respond
to market demands.
With the expansion of the insurance market in 2024, the insurance sector
contributed approximately 1.13% to the national economy, with an insurance density of
around USD 20.65 per capita. Although Cambodia’s insurance penetration rate and
insurance density remained relatively low compared to other countries in the region,
these figures indicated substantial potential for further development, making the market
increasingly attractive to both domestic and foreign investors.
